hints.title: Active Loans Filtering
hints.text: Filter borrowing events to consider only items currently checked out where return date is unrecorded.

hints.title: Group Count Aggregation
hints.text: Aggregate unreturned records per title to tally current active borrowings.

hints.title: Capacity Comparison
hints.text: Keep only titles whose active loan count equals their total inventory quantity, sorting by copies descending.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
SELECT 
    b.book_id,
    b.title,
    b.author,
    b.total_copies
FROM library_books b
JOIN borrowing_records r ON b.book_id = r.book_id
WHERE r.return_date IS NULL
GROUP BY b.book_id, b.title, b.author, b.total_copies
HAVING COUNT(r.record_id) = b.total_copies
ORDER BY b.total_copies DESC, b.book_id ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Joining active borrowing events with book inventories followed by grouping and equality filtering.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries per book recalculate unreturned counts repeatedly.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Filtering return date prior to grouping reduces aggregation volume.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use group filtering with HAVING equality to match total inventory count.

import pandas as pd

def find_books_with_no_available_copies(library_books: pd.DataFrame, borrowing_records: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    active = borrowing_records[borrowing_records['return_date'].isna()]
    borrowed_counts = active.groupby('book_id').size().reset_index(name='active_borrowed')
    merged = library_books.merge(borrowed_counts, on='book_id', how='inner')
    res = merged[merged['active_borrowed'] == merged['total_copies']]
    res = res.sort_values(by=['total_copies', 'book_id'], ascending=[False, True])
    return res[['book_id', 'title', 'author', 'total_copies']]
